conventions.convention: A rational mixed Hodge structure has a finite-dimensional rational underlying space, finite increasing W and finite decreasing F on its complexification. The induced filtrations on Gr^W_n are n-opposed. Morphisms preserve W and F.
Q(r) has weight −2r and Hodge type (−r,−r). Dual filtrations are defined by annihilators of W_{−a−1} and F^{1−p}. Polarizability uses positivity of Q(Cu, conjugate(v)), with C acting by i^{p−q}.
Deligne's I^{p,q} splits W and F over C. Conjugation agrees with the swapped piece only modulo W_{p+q−2}; the original pieces are not asserted to split the conjugate Hodge filtration.

The mixed Hodge complex comparison is an actual W-preserving chain map from K_Q tensor C to K_C, inducing quasi-isomorphisms on every W-graded complex. Those graded complexes have F-strict differentials and pure degree-r cohomology of weight r+w. Filtration bounds may depend on cochain degree.
Cohomological weights use the shifted image filtration W_m H^n(K) = image(H^n(W_{m−n}K) → H^n(K)); the Hodge filtration is the image filtration from F^pK_C.

The weight sequence has E_1^{p,q} = H^{p+q}(Gr^W_{−p}K), of pure weight q, and Gr^W_m H^n = E_2^{n−m,m}. In the first-quadrant cosimplicial case, L_{−p}sK^n is the sum over cosimplicial degrees i ≥ p, and the total differential on K^{p,q} is δ + (−1)^p d.

load_bearing.statement: Every morphism f:H→K of rational mixed Hodge structures is strict for W and F: f(W_nH)=f(H)∩W_nK and f(F^pH_C)=f(H_C)∩F^pK_C for all n,p. Its kernel, image and cokernel, with induced or quotient filtrations, are mixed Hodge structures; Gr^W_n is exact; and a morphism from weights at least n to weights at most n has pure image of weight n.

For every rational cohomological mixed Hodge complex K and every n, H^n(K_Q) carries a mixed Hodge structure with the shifted weight image filtration and Hodge image filtration. Its weight sequence has E_1^{p,q}=H^{p+q}(Gr^W_{−p}K) pure of weight q, degenerates at E_2, and identifies Gr^W_mH^n(K) with E_2^{n−m,m} compatibly with F. Morphisms induce mixed Hodge morphisms. A first-quadrant cosimplicial system of weight-zero rational Hodge complexes with finite degreewise F, strict internal differentials, pure H^q(K^p) of weight q, and filtration-preserving maps compatible with rational comparisons has a simple mixed Hodge complex for L, with Gr^W_qH^n(sK)=E_2^{n−q,q} and weights at most n.

For a rational mixed Hodge structure, put m=p+q and I^{p,q}=(F^p∩W_m)∩((conjugate(F)^q∩W_m)+Σ_{j≥1}(conjugate(F)^{q−j}∩W_{m−j−1})). Projection identifies I^{p,q} with H_m^{p,q}; W_m=⊕_{p+q≤m}I^{p,q} and F^a=⊕_{p≥a}I^{p,q}; every mixed Hodge morphism preserves the pieces. Moreover I^{p,q}+W_{m−2}=σ(I^{q,p})+W_{m−2}.

A rational mixed Hodge structure is a rational vector space with a finite basis, a finite increasing weight filtration W, and a finite decreasing Hodge filtration F on its complexification, such that Gr^W_nH_C=⊕_{p+q=n}(F^pGr^W_nH_C∩conjugate(F)^qGr^W_nH_C) for every integer n, using the induced filtrations. A morphism is rational linear and preserves W and F.

The datum comprises a bounded-below rational cochain complex with degreewise finite increasing W, a complex cochain complex with degreewise finite increasing W and decreasing F, and a W-compatible comparison K_Q tensor C→K_C inducing quasi-isomorphisms on every Gr^W_w. Each graded complex has finite-dimensional cohomology, F-strict differential, and induced rational pure Hodge cohomology H^r of weight r+w.

alerts.finding: F2 attributes proper hypercover descent to 'a bounded-below constructible coefficient complex F'. The cited thm-proper-hypercovers-compute-constructible-derived-cohomology states its result for F ∈ D^b_c(X;k), and repeats that bounded hypothesis in Given. Bounded-below constructible complexes can be unbounded above, so this restatement enlarges the supplier's coefficient domain without supplied justification. The actual applications here use the bounded constant rational coefficient; those applications do not require the enlargement.

seams_checked.note: The logarithmic theorem's F5 and steps 4.1–8.1 use the graded comparison, graded F-strictness, purity of weight r+w, shifted cohomological W, E_2 degeneration, functoriality and strictness consistently with the batch suppliers. Its pole index a gives weights n+a, hence the lower bound n. No reverse supplier dependency is asserted.

The variation definition uses the stated pure, Tate and polarization conventions. Fixed-part F4 and step 2.1 apply W-strictness to a source of weights at least m and a pure weight-m target, obtaining the compactification image and a pure invariant substructure. This preserves the supplier's weight direction and hypotheses; no reverse supplier dependency is asserted.

Proper-weights F3 and step 1.1 supply actual first-quadrant cosimplicial weight-zero Hodge complexes and use Gr^W_qH^n=E_2^{n−q,q}, giving weights at most n. Its class-map proof uses the stated dual and Tate signs. Restriction-image F3 and steps 1.1–2.1 use the exact W-strictness identity and the pure-image criterion. The separate F2 descent coefficient-range mismatch is recorded as an alert and does not misstate this batch's interface.

The nodal-curve example obtains its weight identification through the proper-weights theorem. Its computed E_2^{1,0}=Q and E_2^{0,1}=0 correspond to Gr^W_0H^1 and Gr^W_1H^1 under this batch's shifted convention. The surviving row is type (0,0), consistent with the rational pure-Hodge definition. No reverse supplier dependency is asserted.
